## Meet Paige Cognetti
Paige Cognetti is the Mayor of Scranton, PA. She first ran for mayor as an Independent, in a campaign called “Paige Against the Machine,” for her fight to take on corruption against the local Democratic machine.
As mayor, Paige reformed the office – taking on special interests and battling corruption in City Hall. She turned down the city car, eliminated cash payments, and cut costs, leading to budget surpluses and rapid improvement of the city’s financial position. Paige has balanced the city’s books, brought in new businesses, and cut red tape to foster job growth and new homes getting built. She is continuing to lower costs by taking on special interests like public utilities, properly managing city assets, and adding modern infrastructure to temper rising insurance costs.

I’m running for Congress to take on a corrupt Washington that has left our community behind. Politicians keep getting richer and our costs keep rising. My public service career has been dedicated to rooting out waste, fraud, and abuse in government. I’m ready to take that fight to the place that needs it most: a Washington controlled by special interests and self-serving politicians who put the people last. Nobody works harder than the people of NEPA, and they deserve a government that works as hard as they do.

pages.title: Priorities - Paige Cognetti For Congress
pages.text:
## Priorities
My public service career has been about bringing reform, transparency, and accountability to government. I’m running for Congress to take on corruption and make Washington work as hard as we do. To help reform a broken Washington, I will fight for:
- A Ban on Congressional Stock Trading. No one should be able to use their public office to enrich themselves.
- No Corporate PAC Money. As a candidate and member of Congress I will reject the influence of special interests.
- Audit the Federal Government. I’ve been cutting waste, fraud, and abuse in government for nearly a decade, but we need to do it with a scalpel, not a chainsaw.
- Break up the huge monopolies that hurt our small businesses and raise costs. Bring more competition into our communities by ending the Big Box monopolies that drive small businesses out of our area, give consumers fewer options, and let a few large companies control everything.
- Strengthen unions; make it easier to join and start a union.
- Respect the power of the people via local control and allocate more federal money directly to municipalities and counties.
- Champion small business by understanding how federal choices impact their ability to stay alive — without access to a healthcare marketplace, many people cannot work at the small businesses they love.
- Go after fees that shrink our pocketbooks with a million little cuts, like capping credit card swipe fees.
- Prevent healthcare industry middlemen from denying care and medications prescribed by doctors.
- Reform the insurance system so that when people pay for insurance, they can expect to be protected when something happens – from healthcare to flooding.
- Fight for paid family leave and affordable childcare.
- Reshore manufacturing jobs, including continuing to add more defense manufacturing in Northeastern Pennsylvania.
- Cut red tape, make permitting make sense, allow more businesses to start, grow and thrive. Move faster on infrastructure projects we need for our economic future, from safe streets to bridges to passenger rail.
- Stop broad tariffs that help the big guys and hurt families, create smart targeted tariffs to protect manufacturing here.
Northeastern Pennsylvanians built this country. The coal and shale under our feet have fueled the nation and powered advancement for generations. We know well the promise of innovation and investment that comes with new technology. But we also know better what it looks like when outside corporations steamroll through our cities and towns, take over our land, extract every bit of profit from our people and our resources, and then leave us high and dry. For generations, these companies have made big promises, let us down, and left us to pick up the pieces.
Now it’s data centers.
I’ve spent a lot of time listening to data center developers trying to explain why they should build here. In the rooms I’ve been in and in the projects I’ve seen, there is no project anywhere in NEPA that should move forward.
I won’t let corporate special interests and speculative developers take advantage of our community yet again. If developers want to build in NEPA, they need to follow our rules. This is our home and we’re not for sale.
Stay away from homes, schools and public parks. No sites in a small town, on top of a school district, or in a beloved state park. Construction must happen on brownfields and sites that can’t be developed for residential use.
Total transparency – no hiding behind NDAs. If these companies can’t be honest about who they are and why they’re here, they shouldn’t even be here at all.
No tax breaks for wealthy corporations. At a time when hardworking Pennsylvanians are struggling to pay their bills and fill up their gas tanks, the last people who need more money in their pockets are big companies and their billionaire executives.
Pay their own way and supply their own energy resources. Produce your own energy, don’t poison our water, and don’t jack up utility costs for local businesses and residents.
Built with local union labor. These jobs must go to local union workers and benefit our community.

pages.title: Anti-Corruption Agenda - Paige Cognetti For Congress
pages.text:
## Ban Congressional Stock Trading
Corrupt politicians in both parties have been taking advantage of their constituents’ trust for too long and Congressman Rob Bresnahan is only the newest offender. Members of Congress consistently trade stocks in companies that directly intersect with their work on congressional committees. They sit in classified briefings, hear economic forecasts before the public does, and vote on legislation that can make or break entire industries. This is the definition of public corruption. I don’t own any individual stocks, and if elected, I won’t buy or trade them, period. I will fight to pass a ban on members of Congress trading stocks so that the people of Northeastern Pennsylvania and Americans everywhere don’t have to wonder if their representative is working to serve their community, or to enrich themselves.
## Ban Corporate PAC Donations
Big corporations have too much influence on our politics. They buy our elected leaders, shape our policy, and use our federal government as a tool to protect their interests and push the priorities of working families to the sidelines. Congressman Bresnahan, has taken over $267,000 from these corporate PACs. As a candidate for Congress, I don’t take a dime from corporate PACs. As a member of Congress, I will propose legislation to ban corporate PAC donations to federal campaigns. The meetings our Representatives take and the priorities they fight for should be dictated by what is best for their districts, not a corporate lobbyist coming with a check.
## No Budget, No Pay
Just last year, we had the longest government shutdown in history, lasting 43 days. Hundreds of thousands of federal workers went without paychecks and veterans’ services were delayed. Yet through it all, Congress members continued to collect their salaries without interruption. No ordinary American gets paid when they fail to do their job, and neither should Congress. I will fight to pass a No Budget, No Pay bill to withhold members’ pay until a budget is passed, ensuring that members of Congress feel the consequences of their failures like everyone else does. Northeastern Pennsylvanians work hard and punch the clock to earn their paychecks. Washington shouldn’t be any different.
## Term Limits
Our elected officials are supposed to work for the people they were elected to serve. But too many Washington politicians have forgotten who they work for. There are members of Congress who have gotten too comfortable and have stayed too long. I will fight to pass a constitutional amendment establishing term limits: 18 years for members of the House of Representatives, 18 years for Senators. We should also apply the 18 year standard to Supreme Court justices so that the structure no longer incentivizes Justices to serve well past their ability to do so and the Court ceases to become a place of constant gamesmanship.
## Audit the Government
The federal government spends trillions of our tax dollars every year. The American people are owed a full accounting of every dollar spent in their name. It’s the bare minimum needed to restore trust in our federal government. In Congress, I will fight for a comprehensive, mandatory, independent audit of every federal agency. In Scranton, we made tough decisions with a red pen to turn our city’s finances around. We balanced the budget for the first time in decades and brought our city back from junk bond status to A- credit rating. We need more fiscal responsibility in Washington, and I’ll bring my red pen with me to Congress. A person that can’t account for their spending gets their credit card cut off. Congress should face the same consequences. The federal government audits agencies year after year, but there aren’t meaningful enforcement mechanisms to address findings. I will fight to make sure agencies that fail their audits are legally required to address every finding before Congress approves their next budget.
## Ban Members of Congress from Becoming Lobbyists
Under current law, former members of Congress must wait just one year before lobbying their former colleagues; Senators must wait two. After that, there are virtually no restrictions. Corporations pay a premium for former members of Congress precisely because of their access to and relationships with their former colleagues. After being elected to serve their constituents, these members cash in, further stacking the deck against regular Americans in corporations’ favor. Enough is enough. I will push to permanently ban members of Congress from becoming lobbyists.
## Ban Members of Congress from Serving on Corporate Boards
Current rules technically bar members from being paid for this service, but sitting on a board builds the relationships, loyalties, and goodwill that translate into a lucrative payday the moment they leave office. Former members who land corporate board seats average over $350,000 a year, twice their congressional salary. In Congress, I will fight to pass legislation banning members from serving on corporate boards while in office. Congressional members are elected to serve the people. You cannot do that job while answering to a corporate boardroom.
## Ban Prediction Market Gambling on War, Elections, and Government Activity
Prediction markets have exploded in the past year, offering the wealthy and well-connected a chance to cash in on their insider knowledge of elections, acts of war, and government decisions. As the war in Iran sent financial markets into chaos, insiders were making millions on prediction markets, placing suspiciously-timed bets on military strikes before they happened. Ordinary Americans were watching their retirement accounts take a hit while the well-connected cashed in. It needs to be banned for Members of Congress and their staff.

## “We can’t lower costs or expand access to health care if our politicians are too focused on serving themselves”
Scranton Mayor Paige Cognetti, the Democratic nominee for Congress in Pennsylvania’s 8th U.S. House District, has unveiled an ambitious anti-corruption agenda that traces its roots to how she got her start in politics.
The proposed reform policies would put restrictions on the ways members of Congress can use elected office to enrich themselves. In addition to term limits and withholding lawmakers’ pay during a government shutdown, Cognetti’s agenda would ban Congressional stock trading, prohibit corporate PAC donations and bar lawmakers from making prediction market wagers on war, elections and government activity.

October 30, 2026
## Paige: “Last night at the debate, [Bresnahan] was saying that he ‘has Pennsylvanians in mind.’ He wouldn’t have voted for the Iran War six times, the tariffs eight times, and voted to cut $1 trillion from Medicaid while giving himself a tax break if that were the case.”
SCRANTON, PA – Scranton Mayor and candidate for Congress in Pennsylvania’s 8th Congressional District Paige Cognetti today joined the hosts of MSNOW’s Morning Joe to talk about her record of delivering results for the city of Scranton and all the promises Rob Bresnahan has broken since going down to Washington.
Paige outlined her agenda to lower costs, address the health care crisis that Bresnahan unleashed on NEPA, and hold the corrupt politicians in Washington accountable – just like she did last night on the debate stage in Pittston. On the eve of Halloween, she also discussed just how much more the holiday is costing young families like hers this year – and how she’ll vote to immediately end the cost-spiking Iran War and reckless tariffs as NEPA’s congresswoman.
Mika Brzezinski : “I hear you have daughters. I’m just curious if you’re hearing on the campaign trail from a lot of women about access to health care and life saving health care–what would you be able to do? What would be your Day One focus on costs for health care?”
Paige : “Today I’ve got a couple little girls downstairs getting ready for their Halloween parades, and we’re all complaining about the cost of candy. Sour Patch Kids are up 40%. Hershey’s products are up 25%… You know, and we can laugh in these moments as we’re fighting this fight. But the costs are extreme.
We already have 9,000 people in this five county area in Northeastern Pennsylvania who don’t have access to healthcare. We’re looking at another 20,000 that are going to lose it later today. I’ll be at Moses Taylor Hospital. We are making sure that we keep the doors open as best we can in our hospitals, in Scranton and beyond. But this gutting of Medicaid is making the math not work for hospitals.
“It has only gotten worse, and it’s only going to get worse when these cuts really go into effect. So in Congress in January, we got to put the floor back under Medicaid. The system needs a lot of reform. The ACA was never perfect. We all know that. But we cannot make the reforms that are necessary in health care with millions of Americans off of the insurance rolls.”
Jonathan Lemire : “So, Madam Mayor, you obviously just went through the idea of the cost seem priority for Democrats, were they to take the majority, were you to win in next week’s time. How do you balance that with the call from so many Democrats about accountability, about investigations that should be conducted into the Trump administration, whether the president himself, his family, his cabinet and the like? How do you do both?”
Paige : “Before I was mayor, I was on the Scranton school board and same thing–there was criminal activity happening on the school board. I stood for an appointment, called in the attorney general, who was then [now Governor] Josh Shapiro, and we pushed out that corruption at the Scranton School District. I then worked for the auditor general looking at waste, fraud and abuse across school districts. That’s what I want to do in Congress: get in there, dig in. What are the procurement violations? What are the agencies doing that they shouldn’t be doing? And this, you know, it doesn’t matter which party. The corruption can go either way.
“We need to be able to call it like we see it wherever that corruption happens. We have to go into those oversight processes really focused on how we can make the government work for people.
“The federal government is captured by corporations and billionaires. We all know that the economy is rigged. We need to make sure that we’re doing the oversight in parallel with the things that will meaningfully lower costs: ending the war on Iran, ending the erratic tariffs, and making sure that we’re showing people that we’re serious about working for them.”

pages.title: Letter: Cognetti’s experience, commitment belong in Congress - Paige Cognetti For Congress
pages.text:
July 13, 2026
## Letter: Cognetti’s experience, commitment belong in Congress
Cognetti’s resume of public service is simply outstanding. She served on the Scranton School Board, a thankless task at best, working to bring financial stability and promoting enhanced educational programs for students.
A chance for statewide public service summoned her the office of the Auditor General, where her expertise and talents made immediate and lasting impacts.
By 2019, corruption overwhelmed Scranton city government. The mayor ended up in jail, a shameful episode. Paige was stung by the state of things in City Hall, launching a campaign for mayor as an Independent, pledging to clean up the mess. The Democratic organization opposed her, but her message was clear and was heard by the voters of Scranton. Her majorities in two subsequent elections in which she has run as a Democrat have been overwhelming.
Cognetti is also a wonderful mother to two beautiful children and has been able to balance her responsibilities as a mother with her duties as mayor. Her commitment to improving the quality of peoples’ lives is something we can trust and support without reservation.
I urge you to cast your vote for Paige Cognetti for Congress.

## 27-year police officer: “Cognetti is different. Independent. Does the right thing, no matter what the politicians want”
SCRANTON, PA – Scranton Mayor and candidate for Congress in Pennsylvania’s 8th Congressional District Paige Cognetti is not afraid to stand up for what’s right – even if she stands alone. In her newest ad “ Safety ,” a former police detective who spent 27 years in local law enforcement highlights Paige’s independent record which includes standing up to her own party to invest in law enforcement to keep NEPA safe.
Paige first ran for mayor as an independent against the corrupt Democratic machine in Scranton. As Mayor, she has prioritized what’s best for her community over any political agenda, including standing up to Harrisburg and Washington Democrats to secure more police funding. Now, she’s running for Congress to take on a broken Washington where she’ll always prioritize Pennsylvanians over party.
Bob: You know, I saw a lot as a cop for 27 years.
Scranton was a tough place on the brink of bankruptcy. Corruption all over.
Then, Paige Cognetti came in and took on the Machine.
Fixed the budget, turned down a pay raise, and invested in our safety.
Cognetti stood up to Democrats in Harrisburg and Washington to get more money for the police force.
Over 5 million in funding.
Cognetti is different. Independent. Does the right thing, no matter what the politicians want.
Paige Cognetti lives in Scranton with her husband and two daughters. Prior to her tenure as Mayor, Paige served on the Scranton School Board in 2017 and as a special assistant to the Pennsylvania Auditor General in 2018 where she worked to root out waste, fraud, and abuse in government.
In 2019, Paige ran for mayor of Scranton as an Independent, taking on the local political establishment in a campaign that was referred to as “Paige Against The Machine.” Paige chose to run as an Independent after the then-mayor resigned after pleading guilty to federal bribery, conspiracy and extortion charges. Paige stunned Scranton’s political establishment when she won thanks to her promise to clean up the corruption in Scranton. Paige was the first woman ever elected Scranton Mayor, and was eight months pregnant when she won. Paige ran for reelection as a Democrat in 2021, winning a full term with over 71% of the vote and beating the Machine again. She beat the longtime local Democratic boss with 76% of the vote in the Democratic Primary in May of 2025.
As Mayor of Scranton, Paige has made government reform a top priority. In office she has:
- Turned down the city government car and gas card
- Eliminated cash payments and took on no bid contracts
- Took on utilities and fought big businesses gouging consumers
- Held more than 100 public events across every neighborhood in the city
- Cut red tape, slashing building permit fees
- Led the city’s credit rating to investment-grade status
- Saved millions for taxpayers by refinancing bonds
Paige has reinvigorated the city’s finances and helped attract new businesses while simultaneously laying a solid foundation for a brighter future — restoring confidence through responsible government and reimagining outdated ways of doing business.
Now Paige is running for Congress to clean up corruption in Washington and give the people of NEPA a Congresswoman who will work just as hard as they do. Congressman Bresnahan campaigned on a pledge to ban congressional stock trading, but has instead made more than 600 trades worth millions in assets since arriving in Washington. When pressed by WVIA on why he won’t stop trading stocks while in office, Bresnahan – who has reported assets in the tens of millions – complained that he did not want to “lose money and go broke.” Most recently, unearthed audio revealed that Bresnahan admitted to speaking with his financial advisor about his upcoming stock positions while voting in Congress.
For more on Paige’s campaign, go to PaigeforPA.com.

SCRANTON, PA – Scranton Mayor and candidate for Congress in Pennsylvania’s 8th Congressional District Paige Cognetti has a proven track record of taking on corruption and corporations to stand up for the people. Today, Paige is taking her fight directly to greedy data center developers and stock trading Congressman Rob Bresnahan in her new ad: “ Code .”

No special perks, no secrets, no broken promises. And she calls out Bresnahan, who prioritized his portfolio over NEPA when he “traded AI stock while he pushed for data centers.”
With her new ad, Paige becomes one of the first congressional candidates across the entire country to stand up directly to greedy data center developers and tell them our communities are not for sale — taking on the machine, just like she’s always done.

We know what that’s worth.
We know what it cost.

Now it’s data centers.

You can’t meet that?

I’m Paige Cognetti, and I approve this ad.
This is our home. We are not for sale.
